question: Does real continuous stellar-light morphology improve transferable raw cluster lensing when it redistributes, but never adds, the radial lensing budget; and which placement, scale, contrast, or strength matters most?
pre_score_disclosure: The unscored 0.1 draft used a 128-arcsec FFT half-width and an edge-deflection gate. It was superseded before map construction because a mass-conserving quadrupole has a physical nonzero far-field deflection; 0.2 instead pads the zero-convergence source to 256 arcsec and gates the source edge itself.
All four lens catalogs and prior residuals are spent at project level. The new distinction, F160W maps, processing, formula, grids, split, and gates are frozen before any new lens score.
This is a stellar-light morphology test, not a complete baryonic map. It contains BCG/ICL/member light but no accepted gas surface-density map.
Every known training and held-out multiple-image coordinate is masked identically before smoothing, so target light cannot become a mass predictor.

F160W foreground/background contamination is bounded by radial normalization and the frozen contrast caps, but a multiband membership/stellar-mass map remains a required confirmation after any positive result.

The perturbation has zero annular surface-density mean and an independently subtracted circular deflection mean. Galaxy rotation, radial bridge, and Solar point-mass predictions therefore remain exact parent controls.

formula.circular_closure: Subtract the numerically sampled azimuthal mean of alpha_delta,R at every interpolation radius.

curvature_additive_alpha10.source: locked curvature_additive_alpha10 row from the four-cluster raw transfer

light_template.input: MAST CLASH 65-mas F160W drz plus inverse-variance weight mosaics
light_template.radial_taper: T=1 through 55 arcsec, half-cosine from 55 to 60 arcsec, zero outside 60 arcsec
light_template.background: median of finite positive-weight pixels from 75 to 90 arcsec; only available footprint pixels enter
light_template.invalid_pixel_fill: same-radius median of unmasked positive-weight pixels in 0.5-arcsec annuli
light_template.negative_flux_rule: subtract the frozen background and clip negative flux to zero
light_template.smoothing_boundary: normalized Gaussian convolution of flux and valid-mask weight
light_template.no_photometric_mass_calibration: Only angular weights are used; every radial mass/convergence normalization comes from the pre-existing baryonic parent profile.

factor_grid.zero_fraction_deduplication: One exact control per parent; duplicated zero cells are not rescored.
factor_grid.screen_metric: profiled training-image RMS at the parent's newly refitted zero-f control geometry

systems_and_split.within_family_rule: Hold out the lexicographically last image in each family with at least three images; fit geometry and source positions only to the remaining images.
systems_and_split.selection_rule: For each parent, select the complete-root shortlisted setting with minimum equal-system exact training RMS; ties favor lower f, larger smoothing, lower cap, then carrier order baryonic-extra-full.
systems_and_split.validation_rule: Lock carrier, smoothing, cap, and f; refit only the six ordinary geometry nuisance parameters on each validation cluster's training images, then score its held-out images.

outcome_gates.galaxy_bridge_solar_rule: exactly unchanged from each parent because the perturbation has no angular contrast for the axisymmetric/point-mass controls and zero circular mean for the radial bridge
